WONDER DAILY GRADE 2 · MATH

How much did it grow?

A bean becomes. · Curiosity-led family day

Pretend notebook · height above soil
Day4812
Height8 cm14 cm23 cm

Use the pretend notebook numbers. The picture is not a ruler.

1. On Day 4 it was 8 cm tall. On Day 8 it was 14 cm. How much taller?

14 − 8 = ______Draw or write your thinking.

2. On Day 12 it was 23 cm. In our number story, it later grows 9 cm more. How tall then?

23 + 9 = ______Draw or write your thinking.

3. How many days pass from Day 4 to Day 12? Count the spaces between days.

12 − 4 = ______Draw or write your thinking.

Would every real bean grow this much? No. These numbers are invented for our math story; real growth varies.

GROWN-UP NOTE About 15 min: 3 to compare the picture and table, 9 to draw or calculate, 3 to explain. Use tens-and-ones or number-line hops. Numbers are pretend; do not measure the illustration.
WONDER DAILY GRADE 2 · READING

The quiet work of growing

A bean becomes. · Curiosity-led family day

Name __________________________ Date _______________

Little Wonderer looks at the bean. “Is anything in there?” A tiny plant is tucked inside. Stored food will help it begin.

With water, air, and enough warmth, the bean starts to grow. A root comes out first. It responds to gravity and grows down. A shoot grows up.

Leaves open in the light. They use light, water, and carbon dioxide from the air to make food. The little plant can make more of what it needs.

“It looks the same,” says Little Wonderer. Big Wonderer opens their notebook. An earlier mark is lower than today's tip. Their notes help them see a change.

“Did the bean need leaves to begin?” they wonder. Look inside it again. The tiny plant had stored food before it had open leaves.

They sit together by the window. Growing takes time. “What might change next?” asks Big Wonderer. Little Wonderer has a new question to draw.

Talk together: What helped the bean begin before its leaves opened? How did their notes help them notice growth?

GROWN-UP NOTE About 15 min: look at the scenes, read the six short beats, then talk. Ask what changed in your child's idea. Point, speak, or pause; no independent reading required.

Tell the bean's small story.

Name __________________________ Date _______________

Choose a scene. Look closely, say your idea, then draw or write what the picture helped you understand.

Draw the seed, root, or leaf you chose. Label one part and add an arrow to show what it does.

seed · stored food · root · shoot · leaf · light · water

Inside the bean, … What is kept there?

The root grows … Where does it go? What does it take in?

The leaf uses … What helps it make food?

Read it together. Can you point to the part your words explain? Add a capital letter and an ending mark if you are writing.

GROWN-UP NOTE About 15 min: 3 to choose and talk, 4 to draw, 6 to write 1–3 sentences, 2 to read back. Accept invented spelling, speech, or dictation. One careful idea is enough.
